 South Indian Bank Q2 net profit rises 21% to INR 426 crore, gross NPA falls to 1.24%
 #Taxation & Finance News #Commercial #India 
 Last Updated : 20 Oct 2026

 Synopsis
 South Indian Bank reported a 21% year-on-year rise in net profit to INR 426 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with INR 351 crore in the year-ago period. Total income increased to INR 3,264 crore, while interest income rose to INR 2,796 crore. The Kerala-based lender's gross non-performing assets declined to 1.24% of gross advances from 2.93% a year earlier. Net NPAs also improved to 0.09% from 0.56%, although provisions and contingencies increased to INR 159 crore during the quarter. 
 Representative image
 South Indian Bank reported a 21% year-on-year increase in net profit to INR 426 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with INR 351 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. 
The Kerala-based private sector lender's total income rose to INR 3,264 crore in the September quarter from INR 2,923 crore a year earlier, according to its regulatory filing. 
Interest income increased to INR 2,796 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with INR 2,407 crore in the same period of the previous financial year. 
The bank also reported an improvement in asset quality. Gross non-performing assets (NPAs) declined to 1.24% of gross advances at the end of September 2026, from 2.93% a year earlier. 
Net NPAs fell to 0.09% at the end of September 2026, compared with 0.56% in the corresponding month of the previous year. 
However, provisions and contingencies increased to INR 159 crore in the September quarter, from INR 63 crore in the same quarter of the previous financial year. 
The decline in gross and net NPAs indicates an improvement in the bank's reported asset quality compared with the previous year. However, the increase in provisions and contingencies remains a figure to watch alongside income and profitability in subsequent quarters. The bank's future performance will depend on its ability to sustain earnings growth while managing loan quality and credit-related costs.
